facts.text: Park Hyatt Tokyo occupies the 39th to 52nd floors of Shinjuku Park Tower, in Shinjuku on the west side of Tokyo.
facts.excerpt: Located on the west side of Tokyo in Shinjuku, Park Hyatt Tokyo occupies the 39th to 52nd floors of Shinjuku Park Tower

facts.text: Shinjuku Park Tower was designed by Pritzker Prize-winner Kenzo Tange.
facts.excerpt: Shinjuku Park Tower, a modern Japanese architectural masterpiece designed by Pritzker Prize-winner Kenzo Tange

facts.text: The Library on the 41st floor holds more than 2,000 hand-selected books.
facts.excerpt: Nestled on the 41st floor, The Library includes more than 2,000 hand-selected books on art, culture, history and more.

facts.text: The indoor pool at Club On The Park has panoramic views of Tokyo and Mt. Fuji through floor-to-ceiling glass walls.
facts.excerpt: sweeping panoramic views of Tokyo and Mt. Fuji through floor-to-ceiling glass walls

facts.text: Club On The Park is a two-story skylit spa and fitness center.
facts.excerpt: Club On The Park is a two-story skylit oasis with a 2,100-square-meter (22,600-square-foot) spa and fitness center

facts.text: New York Grill has an open kitchen, live jazz, a 360-degree Tokyo view and murals by Italian artist Valerio Adami.
facts.excerpt: Crowning the hotel with an interactive open kitchen, live jazz performances heard throughout, a captivating 360-degree Tokyo view, and two vibrant New York inspired murals by Italian artist Valerio Adami

facts.text: New York Bar has nightly jazz performances with a Tokyo night view as the backdrop.
facts.excerpt: Connected to New York Grill, nightly jazz performances, a captivating Tokyo night view as the stage backdrop

facts.text: Girandole by Alain Ducasse is a French brasserie with a double-level collage of 144 black-and-white photographs by Vera Mercer.
facts.excerpt: An iconic double-level collage of 144 black-and-white photographs by Vera Mercer, celebrates European café life.

facts.text: The Peak Lounge & Bar serves afternoon tea in a glass atrium surrounded by a bamboo grove with views of Mt. Fuji.
facts.excerpt: By day, enjoy an artfully redefined afternoon tea set in a spectacular glass atrium surrounded by a serene bamboo grove with unparalleled views of Mt. Fuji.

facts.text: On a clear winter day, Mt. Fuji can be seen from each dining table at Kozue.
facts.excerpt: On a clear winter day, views of Mt. Fuji can be seen from each dining table.

facts.text: Kozue is closed on Wednesdays, except on national holidays.
facts.excerpt: Kozue will be closed on Wednesdays, except on national holidays.

facts.text: Room service is available 24 hours.
facts.excerpt: For your dining pleasure and convenience, 24-hour service is available.

facts.text: A complimentary shuttle runs daily between the hotel's main entrance and Shinjuku station every 30 minutes.
facts.excerpt: A complimentary shuttle (maximum 9 passengers) service departs daily from the hotel's main entrance to Shinjuku station every 30 minutes

facts.text: A taxi or hired car from Haneda Airport takes approximately 45 minutes, depending on traffic.
facts.excerpt: Taxis are available and will take approximately 45 minutes, depending on traffic.

facts.text: The hotel reopened on December 9, 2025 after a 19-month renovation.
facts.excerpt: thoroughly reinterpreted during a 19-month renovation. It reopened December 9, 2025.

facts.text: The renovation was by Paris's Studio Jouin Manku.
facts.excerpt: Two months shy of that milestone, the icon closed for a gentle yet noticeably graceful renovation by Paris

facts.text: The hotel featured in the 2003 film Lost in Translation.
facts.excerpt: International fanfare came after its starring turn in 2003

facts.text: The walnut library is unaltered down to the placement of each book as designer John Morford first arranged them.
facts.excerpt: The walnut library is unaltered down to the exact placement of each tome as the designer first arranged them

facts.text: Cribs, high chairs and kids' menus are available, and kids under 12 stay free.
facts.excerpt: Cribs, high chairs and kids

facts.text: The pool is not available to kids under three.
facts.excerpt: the pool is not available to kids under three

facts.text: Meiji Jingu shrine in Yoyogi Park is a 15-20 minute walk south.
facts.excerpt: just a 15-20 minute straight shot south on foot

facts.text: Rooms feature curated artwork, bespoke furnishings and views of Tokyo.
facts.excerpt: Each space features curated artwork, bespoke furnishings and breathtaking views of Tokyo

facts.text: 1 King Bed rooms on the 43rd and 44th floors have an obstructed view and no city view.
facts.excerpt: this room has an obstructed view and does not offer a city view

facts.text: New York Bar is a must do on Tokyo's bucket list.
